title: select() attaches an undischarged machine-intent requirement, turning green experiment suites UNKNOWN
summary: Any select() in a function executed via mncs experiment run resolves every case correctly yet reports suite UNKNOWN ('compilation retained required unresolved obligations'): the frontend attaches a realization-branchless machine-intent requirement no backend discharges, and the experiment contract counts it required. mncs.test's own assertions use select pervasively, so the framework idiom and the experiment contract disagree.
requiredBehavior: Either supported backends discharge the branchless-select requirement, or the toolchain names select in the unresolved-obligation diagnostic, or the contract documents select as unavailable on the experiment path. Silent all-cases-met UNKNOWN must go.

reproducer.text: Two kernels with identical semantics over identical corpus shapes: select variant UNKNOWN, branch variant PASS. See mncs-lab pressure/reproducers/select-unknown/.

observation.summary: Minimal select/branch pair reproduces the UNKNOWN at mncs-language 066897e on portable-WASM.

reproduction.instructions: Run both reproducer kernels via mncs experiment run; select variant is UNKNOWN with all cases met, branch variant PASS.

evidence.summary: select kernel: 2/2 cases met, suite UNKNOWN, machine-intent obligations retained.
branch kernel: 2/2 cases met, suite PASS, no obligations.
mncs.lab.variants uses a plain-branch helper; lab-variant corpus PASS on wasm+bytecode (LAB-EXP-001).

workaround.description: Lab kernels avoid select() on experiment-run paths (labeled use-site comment). mncs test paths still use select via mncs.test.assertions.
